mobile.guide.helpIntro: Learn to record your workout and contact your coach.
mobile.guide.invite.title: Your first workout, step by step
mobile.guide.invite.body: We will guide you through this real session. Open an exercise to see your coach's instructions and video. You can pause or skip this guide and return from More → Help.
mobile.guide.record.title: Targets and actual results
mobile.guide.record.body: The values above the fields are targets. Enter what you actually did in the editable fields, using their units. Record only what you know; you do not need to fill everything in or copy the targets.
mobile.guide.save.title: Save a real set
mobile.guide.save.body: After entering your results, tap Save set on that set. The guide will continue after it is saved. An empty field is not zero. You can keep training without a connection.
mobile.guide.sync.title: Saving and synchronization
mobile.guide.sync.body: Records are saved on this phone before they are sent. If any are pending, reopen this session with a connection or tap Retry. Do not clear app data while records are pending.

mobile.guide.sync.synced: There are no records waiting to be sent in this session.
mobile.guide.sync.conflict: A record needs review. Check the notice: it has not been marked as synchronized. Ask your coach if you need help.
mobile.guide.help.title: Finish and ask for help when you need it
mobile.guide.help.body: When you finish training, return to the list and tap Finish day to rate the session effort. Use Comments for an exercise question or incident, or message your coach in Chat. Opening these options sends nothing. Completing the guide does not finish your workout.

coach.routine.advancedTechnique.topSet.d:
Your main heavy set for the day. After warm-up, perform one top set at the heaviest load you can handle for the target rep range with solid technique.

e.g. On bench press, after build-up sets, your heaviest set of 5 reps at 100 kg.
coach.routine.advancedTechnique.backOffS:
Sets performed after the top set. Reduce the load slightly (typically 10–20%) to accumulate more volume with controlled fatigue.

e.g. If your top set was 100 kg, do the next 2 sets at 85 kg for 8–10 reps.
coach.routine.advancedTechnique.clusterS:
Split a normal set into small rep blocks with very short rests (10–30 s) between them. This lets you move a heavy load for more total reps than you could in one continuous set.

e.g. Instead of 6 consecutive squat reps, do 2, rest 15 s, 2, rest 15 s, then the last 2.
Maximize fiber recruitment in little time. Perform an initial set near failure, rest 10–15 s, then do mini-sets of a few reps with the same load until you cannot hit the target number.

e.g. 15 leg extension reps, rest 10 s, do 3, rest 10 s, do 3… until you can only do 2.
Push past initial failure. Work to failure, reduce the load (often 20–30%), and continue for as many reps as possible.

e.g. Biceps curl with 20 kg to failure, grab 14 kg and keep repping.

client.nutrition.considerations.title: Highlights
client.nutrition.considerations.high_pro: High in protein, a key nutrient to repair and strengthen muscle.
Strong protein contribution to support recovery and muscle mass.
High in protein, a macronutrient that also helps with satiety.
client.nutrition.considerations.low_prot: Modest protein contribution; pair it with other sources to complete the meal.
Low in protein, better combined with denser protein foods.
Not a protein standout; it mainly contributes other macronutrients.
client.nutrition.considerations.high_car: A direct energy source for daily activity and training.
Carbohydrates predominate, the body's main fuel.
Provides carbohydrates to maintain energy and refill glycogen.
client.nutrition.considerations.low_carb: Very low in carbohydrates, with a minimal impact on energy stores.
Reduced carbohydrate content, useful for managing daily energy load.
Barely contributes carbs, so it fits easily into lower-carb plans.
client.nutrition.considerations.healthy_: Contains good-quality fats that support normal body function.
Stands out for its unsaturated fat profile, beneficial for heart health.
A source of healthy fats that also help absorb some vitamins.
client.nutrition.considerations.high_sat: High saturated fat; worth factoring in when planning the rest of the day.
A considerable saturated fat concentration, better eaten in moderation.
Saturated fats make up a high share of its total fat.
client.nutrition.considerations.high_sal: High sodium; consider moderating the portion if you are watching salt.
High salt concentration from processing, curing or seasoning.
Adds a notable amount of sodium to the daily total.
client.nutrition.considerations.high_sug: Contains fast-absorbing sugars that provide immediate energy.
A notable amount of simple sugars; better used at specific times.
High sugar concentration to keep in mind for a balanced intake.
client.nutrition.considerations.high_fib: High in fiber, a key element for digestion and gut transit.
A high fiber contribution that helps keep you fuller for longer.
Excellent fiber content, supporting a more gradual energy release.
client.nutrition.considerations.high_cal: High energy density; it packs a lot of energy into a small portion.
A very energy-dense option, useful when calorie needs are high.
High calorie concentration, so portion size should match your goal.
client.nutrition.considerations.low_calo: Very low in calories, useful for adding volume without much energy.
A light option with a low energy contribution, easy to include.
Reduced calorie content, ideal when you want a bigger plate.
client.nutrition.considerations.micronut: Stands out for its natural contribution of essential micronutrients.
Provides vitamins and minerals with relevant nutritional value.
A notable micronutrient contribution that complements the food profile.
client.nutrition.considerations.low_salt: Clean profile: low in added sugars and sodium.
Moderate in salt and simple sugars.
Low in added sugars and salt, easy to fit into a controlled plan.
client.nutrition.considerations.empty_ca: Low nutrient density: energy with little satiety.
Calorie contribution with little fiber, protein or micronutrients.
A low-satiety energy profile; better paired with more nutritious foods.
client.nutrition.considerations.low_satu: Low in saturated fat, with a lighter fat profile.
Reduced saturated fat, suitable for a leaner pattern.
A contained saturated fraction, easy to include in a balanced plan.
client.nutrition.considerations.low_suga: Low in simple sugars, with a more contained glucose impact.
Reduced sugar content, useful for a steadier intake.
Little simple sugar in the serving.
client.nutrition.considerations.balanced: A nutritionally balanced plate with a suitable macro split.
Keeps a balanced distribution of carbs, protein and fat.
Macro profile aligned with a complete, balanced plate.
client.nutrition.considerations.dominant: More than half of the energy comes from fat.
A fat-dominant plate; adjust the portion to the day's goal.
Macro imbalance: a high share of calories from fat.
client.nutrition.considerations.vegetabl: A relevant vegetable base with antioxidants and micronutrients.
Includes a notable contribution of vegetables and micronutrients.
Vegetable content that adds volume, fiber and micronutrients.
